_what: Numbers of the account files' first byte store at a computer (new_account_files, src/account_files/bind.rs `NewAccountFiles`: the id of the origin record a new account gets, its rank, the vault service and field its secret is held under as a SigV4 signing root), byte release, name retirement, results and WebDAV folder (src/account_files/settings.rs reads this once). release (src/account_files/release.rs, old trillion src/namespace-byte-release.json): candidates_per_page and keys_per_page bound one page of noting files and of claiming objects; claim_walk is the most waiting rows one claim reads to find claimable ones; recorded_margin_seconds covers clocks that differ between the writer and this store: bytes written are recorded only when no release of the same object was claimed, or finished after the write began minus this margin; claim_stale_minutes is how long a removal that never reported back stays claimed before it is tried again. retire (src/account_files/names.rs retire_names, old trillion src/namespace-set-aside.json items_per_request): the most names one call retires. results (src/account_files/results.rs, old trillion src/namespace-results.mjs): max_value_bytes the largest kept value, page_bytes the most value bytes one page carries, default_page_limit and max_page_limit a page's rows, max_write the most results one write keeps, max_many the most files one many-at-once read names, fields_most the most fields one fields read names, produced_by_chars the most characters kept of who produced a result, reads_at_once_per_caller the reads one caller may have open at once and read_counts_for_ms how long an open read counts if it never finishes. described (src/account_files/write.rs `write_described_spans`, `expire_abandoned_upload`): spans_per_page is how many described chunk spans one record holds; one span is about 140 bytes of JSON (a 16-digit ordinal key, offset, length and a 67-character chunk id), so 1024 spans are about 140 KB, under the 1 MiB record bound (src/records.rs MAX_RECORD_BYTES). open_upload_expiry_days is how long an upload may stay open without a finish or cancel before a later start cancels it: 7 days: the S3 user guide's abort-incomplete-multipart-upload lifecycle example (DaysAfterInitiation 7, section 'Aborting incomplete multipart uploads using a bucket lifecycle policy'); tus protocol 1.0.0 leaves the expiry to the server and announces it in its Upload-Expires header. transfer (src/account_files/settings.rs `call_deadline`, src/account_files/objects.rs) idle_seconds is the longest one socket read or write may wait for progress before it is refused, for every store request; outer_cap_seconds is the total a stream call (one with content_base64) may take, against a slow drip. chunks (src/account_files/paged_spans.rs `chunks-v1`) bytes is the most bytes one stored chunk object holds: a known-length upload is cut into chunks of at most this size (any length, cut by content), each one object keyed by its BLAKE3; at most the 32 MiB range read bound (objects.rs MAX_RANGE_BYTES). dav (src/account_files/dav.rs, old trillion src/namespace-dav.mjs LIST_LIMIT): list_limit the most entries one folder listing answers, list_page the names read per page while listing; the writable half (src/account_files/dav_write.rs): put_most_bytes the most bytes one PUT keeps (never more than the account files' write of 16 MiB), carry_step the steps one carry call of a MOVE, COPY or DELETE takes and carry_calls the most carry calls one request makes before it answers 503 and resumes when asked again; lock_default_seconds how long a LOCK lasts when it asks no time and lock_most_seconds the longest it may last before it is refreshed. read.parallel_pieces is the most ranged reads of one window in flight at once (a file kept as 32 KiB pages costs one read per page): 32 is one 1 MiB window of such pages. It is a starting bound for the core's measured read rate (concurrency = round-trip time x wanted rate), to be set from the measurement against the real store, not a limit the store gives.
